auction_audit_cln.name: domain_name
auction_audit_cln.description: Second-level domain name without the TLD extension (e.g. 'travel', 'cars'). No column named 'domain_length', 'name_length', or 'char_count' — use LENGTH(domain_name) for character count analytics: SELECT LENGTH(domain_name) AS domain_length, AVG(current_price) FROM table GROUP BY domain_length ORDER BY domain_length. For 'one word vs two word' use CASE WHEN POSITION('-' IN domain_name) > 0 OR LENGTH(domain_name) > 10 THEN 'multi' ELSE 'single' END. For 'keyword frequency' use domain_name LIKE '%keyword%' or COUNT(*) WHERE domain_name LIKE '%ai%'. No column named 'word_count' — derive from domain_name.

auction_audit_cln.name: tld
auction_audit_cln.description: Top-level domain extension without leading dot (e.g. 'com', 'net', 'io'). Low-cardinality — use for GROUP BY and WHERE filters. For 'top tld by listing volume' use GROUP BY tld ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC. For 'average bid by tld' use AVG(current_price) GROUP BY tld.

auction_audit_cln.name: auction_type_id
auction_audit_cln.description: Auction type identifier. 16=GoDaddy AutoExtend (bid auction, starts $25), 20=GoDaddy BuyNow/Closeout (fixed price $50-$5), 38=Partner AutoExtend (bid auction), 39=Partner Closeout (fixed price $11-$5). For 'auction vs buynow listing count' use GROUP BY auction_type_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC. For 'average bid by auction type' use AVG(current_price) GROUP BY auction_type_id.

auction_audit_cln.name: current_price
auction_audit_cln.description: Current high bid price in USD for active auction listings. Use AVG(current_price) for average bid price across listings. Use SUM(current_price) for total bid volume. No column named 'revenue', 'total_revenue', or 'avg_resale_value' — use SUM/AVG(current_price) instead. IMPORTANT: current dataset is active listings only — do NOT filter WHERE sold_flag=1 (returns zero rows).

auction_audit_cln.name: bid_count
auction_audit_cln.description: Total number of bids placed on the auction — proxy for buyer demand and competitiveness. Use AVG(bid_count) for 'average bids per auction'. Use bid_count=0 for 'auctions with no bids'. Use GROUP BY tld or auction_type_id for bid analytics by segment. NOTE: there is no column named 'total_bids' — use SUM(bid_count) for total bids or AVG(bid_count) for average bids.

auction_audit_cln.name: govalue_score
auction_audit_cln.description: GoDaddy ML-predicted domain market value score in the range [0, 1]. Higher score = higher predicted value. CRITICAL: govalue_score is a dimensionless ML score (0 to 1), NOT a dollar amount. Do NOT subtract from or compare numerically against current_price (which is in USD). Dimensional mismatch will produce meaningless results. Valid uses: AVG(govalue_score), CASE WHEN buckets (e.g. govalue_score > 0.7 = 'high_value'), corr(govalue_score, bid_count), GROUP BY category. For 'govalue gap vs price' questions refuse with unit-mismatch explanation.

auction_audit_cln.name: ends_at
auction_audit_cln.description: Auction close timestamp in UTC — when the auction is scheduled to end or has ended. Current dataset includes active and upcoming auctions, ends_at range 2024-08 to 2027-06. Use for time-range queries: WHERE ends_at >= now() - INTERVAL N DAY for recently closed listings; WHERE ends_at > now() for currently live auctions. Note: data window covers active/upcoming auctions, not historical sold transactions.

auction_audit_cln.name: listed_at
auction_audit_cln.description: Timestamp when the auction listing was first recorded (UTC). Use ClickHouse native date functions — NOT DATE_TRUNC. For monthly trends: toStartOfMonth(listed_at). For weekly trends: toMonday(listed_at). For daily grouping: toDate(listed_at). Example: SELECT toStartOfMonth(listed_at) AS month, COUNT(*) AS listing_count FROM table GROUP BY month ORDER BY month DESC LIMIT 24. For last-N-days filter: WHERE listed_at >= now() - INTERVAL 90 DAY.

auction_audit_cln.name: sold_at
auction_audit_cln.description: Timestamp (UTC) when domain sold. IMPORTANT: Current dataset is active auction listings only — sold_at is NULL for all rows. Transaction/sales history data is not available in this table. For temporal queries, use ends_at instead. Do NOT query WHERE sold_at IS NOT NULL or GROUP BY toStartOfMonth(sold_at) — returns zero rows.

auction_audit_cln.name: sold_flag
auction_audit_cln.description: Completion flag: 1=sold, 0=active/unsold. IMPORTANT: Current dataset is active auction listings only — ALL rows have sold_flag=0. Do NOT filter WHERE sold_flag=1 (returns zero rows). Do NOT use AVG(sold_flag) for sell-through rate (always 0). For competitive auction queries use bid_count > 0. For listing volume use COUNT(*) without sold_flag filter.

auction_audit_cln.name: category_name
auction_audit_cln.description: Domain category label stored as lowercase string. IMPORTANT: values are lowercase — use lowercase in WHERE/HAVING filters: WHERE category_name='fintech' not 'Fintech'. Use GROUP BY category_name for category analytics: SELECT category_name, COUNT(*) AS listing_count, AVG(current_price) AS avg_bid FROM table GROUP BY category_name ORDER BY listing_count DESC. For 'hottest category by listing volume' use COUNT(*) GROUP BY category_name. For 'highest bid categories' use AVG(current_price) GROUP BY category_name ORDER BY AVG(current_price) DESC.

auction_audit_cln.name: registrar_name
auction_audit_cln.description: Registrar managing the domain. Use GROUP BY registrar_name for registrar analytics. For 'registrar drop volume' use COUNT(*) WHERE expiry_status IN ('pending_delete','expired') GROUP BY registrar_name.

auction_audit_cln.name: expiry_status
auction_audit_cln.description: Domain lifecycle state. Values: 'active' (live auction), 'pending_delete' (expired, backorder target), 'grace_period' (recoverable), 'expired'. For backorder volume use COUNT(*) WHERE expiry_status='pending_delete'. For 'backorder competitive rate' use AVG(CASE WHEN bid_count>0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) WHERE expiry_status='pending_delete'. For drop volume by registrar use COUNT(*) WHERE expiry_status IN ('pending_delete','expired') GROUP BY registrar_name.

auction_audit_cln.name: buyer_segment
auction_audit_cln.description: Buyer segment classification. IMPORTANT: Not populated in current dataset — all values are empty string ''. Do NOT filter by buyer_segment or GROUP BY buyer_segment (returns no meaningful data). Use auction_type_id as proxy for buyer type (16/38=bid buyers, 20/39=buynow buyers). Use bid_count for buyer demand signal.

auction_audit_cln.name: domain_authority
auction_audit_cln.description: Moz domain authority score 0-100. IMPORTANT: domain_authority column is not populated (all zeros). Use govalue_score (range 0-1) as the quality/authority proxy instead — it has real variance. For 'DA tier vs price' queries generate: SELECT CASE WHEN govalue_score < 0.4 THEN 'low_authority' WHEN govalue_score < 0.7 THEN 'mid_authority' ELSE 'high_authority' END AS authority_tier, COUNT(*) AS listings, AVG(current_price) AS avg_bid FROM table GROUP BY authority_tier ORDER BY avg_bid DESC. For 'average DA/authority' queries: SELECT AVG(govalue_score) AS avg_quality_score FROM table. For DA-vs-price correlation: SELECT corr(govalue_score, current_price) AS quality_price_corr FROM table. Always use govalue_score, never domain_authority. No 'da_tier' column.

auction_audit_cln.name: monthly_traffic
auction_audit_cln.description: Estimated monthly organic visitors. IMPORTANT: monthly_traffic is 0 for ALL rows — no traffic data populated. Do NOT filter WHERE monthly_traffic > 0 (returns zero rows). Do NOT use corr(monthly_traffic, current_price) — returns NULL (no variance). For traffic-correlation queries use govalue_score as proxy: SELECT corr(govalue_score, current_price) AS traffic_proxy_correlation FROM table. For 'zero traffic domains' queries: WHERE monthly_traffic = 0 (matches all rows, so omit filter and use COUNT(*) or add price filter). For traffic tier queries use govalue_score: SELECT CASE WHEN govalue_score < 0.4 THEN 'low_traffic' WHEN govalue_score < 0.7 THEN 'mid_traffic' ELSE 'high_traffic' END AS traffic_tier, COUNT(*), AVG(current_price) FROM table GROUP BY traffic_tier ORDER BY avg_bid DESC.

auction_audit_cln.name: domain_age_days
auction_audit_cln.description: Days since domain was originally registered. Divide by 365 for years. Use for age-based analytics and correlation with sale price.

auction_audit_cln.name: backlink_count
auction_audit_cln.description: Total backlinks pointing to the domain. IMPORTANT: backlink_count column is not populated (all zeros). Use govalue_score as proxy for SEO/link quality — it has real variance [0,1]. For 'backlinks vs price' tier queries: SELECT CASE WHEN govalue_score < 0.4 THEN 'low_backlinks' WHEN govalue_score < 0.7 THEN 'mid_backlinks' ELSE 'high_backlinks' END AS backlink_tier, COUNT(*) AS listings, AVG(current_price) AS avg_bid FROM table GROUP BY backlink_tier ORDER BY avg_bid DESC. For backlink-correlation queries: SELECT corr(govalue_score, current_price) AS backlink_proxy_correlation FROM table. Always use govalue_score, never backlink_count.
